# Reproducible Analysis

An analysis is reproducible when **every number a reader can see was produced by a command they can
re-run**, and nothing was typed by hand into prose. [[labour-fraud-analysis]] is the most complete
instance in the source set, and it gets there through five separate mechanisms rather than one.

## The five mechanisms

**1. One seed for the whole world.** Every generated value in the synthetic dataset descends from a
single committed string, hashed per namespace and key — [[deterministic-seeded-substitution]].

> "Global seed — flip this and re-run to regenerate a completely different (but internally
> consistent) fictional world. Committed value gives the published data."
> — labour-fraud-analysis-a-forensic-data-investigation/src/fiction.py, 2026-07-11

**2. A seed for anything else that samples.** The entity graph's force-directed layout is pinned in
both the dashboard and the notebook, so the same picture comes out twice — see [[networkx]].

**3. No hard-coded numbers, stated as a rule in both directions.** The generators say it:

> "Run after anonymize.py so the numbers always match data/. No hard-coded counts."
> — labour-fraud-analysis-a-forensic-data-investigation/src/build_docs.py, 2026-07-11

and so does the presentation layer — "All figures compute live from the CSVs — nothing is
hard-coded" (`src/app.py`).

**4. Generated artefacts committed and then diff-gated.** The schema, data dictionary, coverage
report and a row-count manifest are regenerated and compared byte-for-byte in CI:
[[generated-docs-checked-by-ci-diff]] and [[generated-audit-artifact]].

**5. The notebook is executed, not just stored.** CI runs it end-to-end headless through `nbconvert`
with a timeout. A notebook that is only ever read is a screenshot; a notebook that must execute on a
clean runner is a test. See [[github-actions]].

## Reproducibility of the analysis, not of the environment

This is the honest boundary, and it is worth stating because the two are routinely confused.

| Reproducible | Enforced by |
|---|---|
| the dataset from a seed | `fiction.py`, `anonymize.py` |
| every derived doc and count | [[make]] `docs` + CI `git diff --exit-code` |
| every figure in the notebook | CI notebook execution |
| structural integrity of the data | `build_db.py` with foreign keys on, plus the test suite |

| **Not** reproducible | Why |
|---|---|
| the Python environment | all twelve dependencies are floor-pinned with `>=`, no upper bound, no lockfile — under a comment claiming reproducibility |
| the declared version floor | the project declares support from 3.10; CI runs 3.12 only, so the floor is never exercised. See [[setuptools-and-pyproject]] |
| the pipeline end-to-end | `make all` needs the private source corpus, which exists on one machine |

A pinned seed makes the *output* deterministic given an environment. It says nothing about the
environment. Both halves are needed and only one is present here.

## The unusual part: testing that a finding survived

Two of the tests assert that the **analytical signals themselves** still exist in the published data
after anonymisation — the shared-contact concentration and the bulk-permit batching. Most pipelines
test that the data is well-formed; this one tests that the data is still *interesting*. See
[[shared-identifier-clustering]] and [[structure-preserving-anonymisation]].

The floors are deliberately loose — the shared-inbox test passes at five, where the dataset actually
shows twenty-three. A regression test with a loose floor catches catastrophic loss of signal without
freezing an exact number into the suite. That is the right trade for a generated dataset and the
wrong one for a claim about magnitude.

## The contrast case

[[data-warehousing-and-business-intelligence]] writes verification queries into its load scripts —
[[verify-the-load-dont-declare-it]] — but commits **no output, no log, no expected-count file**, and
has no Makefile and no CI. Its one genuinely reproducible artefact is the standalone Python reference
script, seeded for exactly this reason: {{reference-implementation-as-specification}}. The discipline
is present as prose there and as machinery here.
